overview: Two functional types of neurons, distinguished by the direction information travels — toward the central nervous system or away from it.
genZNote: Sensory neuron: carries the 'what's happening' report inward. Motor neuron: carries the 'do this' command outward.

aspects.label: Direction of Impulse
aspects.valueA: Carries impulses from receptors toward the central nervous system (afferent).
aspects.valueB: Carries impulses from the central nervous system to effectors like muscles/glands (efferent).

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: A neuron carrying a 'hot surface' signal from skin to the spinal cord.
aspects.valueB: A neuron carrying a 'contract' signal from the spinal cord to a hand muscle.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: In a reflex arc, the sequence is always: receptor → sensory neuron → relay/association neuron → motor neuron → effector — a heavily diagrammed exam sequence.
overlay.memoryTrick: Sensory = Afferent = Arrives at the CNS. Motor = Efferent = Exits the CNS.
overlay.commonMisconception: A single reflex arc pathway is not made of only sensory and motor neurons — most reflex arcs also involve at least one relay (interneuron) in between.
